slot.brief: Body cools from one temperature range to another in a given time; using Newton's law of cooling, find the time for a second (stated) temperature drop in the same surroundings.

stem: A body in surroundings at $20^\circ\text{C}$ cools from $84^\circ\text{C}$ to $52^\circ\text{C}$ in $6$ min. Assuming Newton’s law of cooling holds, how long will it take to cool further to $28^\circ\text{C}$?

verdicts.working: Excess temperature falls from 84−20=64°C to 52−20=32°C in 6 min, halving. To reach 28°C, the excess must fall from 32°C to 8°C, two halvings, taking 12 min.

working:
$e^{-6k}=\dfrac{52-20}{84-20}=\dfrac12$; $e^{-kt}=\dfrac{28-20}{52-20}=\dfrac14$; $t=6\dfrac{\ln4}{\ln2}=12$ min

Independent check: Excess temperature falls from 84−20=64°C to 52−20=32°C in 6 min, halving. To reach 28°C, the excess must fall from 32°C to 8°C, two halvings, taking 12 min.
solution:
By Newton’s law of cooling, the excess temperature halves every $6$ min: $
\frac{52-20}{84-20}=\frac12$.
From $52^\circ\text{C}$ to $28^\circ\text{C}$, the excess temperature falls from $32^\circ\text{C}$ to $8^\circ\text{C}$, i.e. two halvings; hence $t=2(6)=12$ min.
